payload.text: **dc's lessons of 2026-09-17.** (1) A `(non-test)` AT row holds only `n/a` (`AtStatus::permitted_for`): a doc, eyeball or gate row carries no test result, and its satisfaction is `intent ac satisfy` on the criterion. `at edit --kind` re-enters the status through `AtStatus::entry`, so a re-kind is one write. A peer's premise about a model is read in the model's code before any store write: vc's "both to-write" was inverted, and dc's own draft had it too. (2) An invariant arm built on a proxy must exclude what the invariant allows: "no ref shares a def's name and line" flagged `File.close(file)` on the `defp close(file)` line, a real call. (3) A worktree's stash is the repository's stash, and `git stash` refuses intent-to-add entries: a one-shot stash, apply and pop rebase failed halfway, and its pop could have taken an unrelated old stash. Rebase in plain steps: capture the files, reset, check out, `git merge-file`. (4) Homebrew's trust store moves under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, so read it with `brew trust --json=v1`. `spctl --type execute` rejects every bare CLI binary; notarisation shows under `--type open --context context:primary-signature` (vc measured). (5) A fully-qualified `brew install tap/name/formula` trusts the formula itself (install.rb:197), and a short name is refused until it is trusted.
